ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and material counterparties against: (i) FINTRAC politically exposed person (PEP) definitions under PCMLTFA and SOR/2002-184, covering foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and heads of international organizations, with enhanced due diligence for all foreign PEPs; (ii) the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List); (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) the Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List administered by Global Affairs Canada under SEMA and the United Nations Act; and (v) domestic criminal watchlists and B.C. Corporate Registry sanctions screening. Verification requires primary-source identification documents (notarized passport and corporate registry extract), a Medium-Risk Enhanced AML tier designation, ongoing transaction monitoring on all documentary letter-of-credit and SWIFT/TT payment flows, and a minimum five-year record-retention period under PCMLTFA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: British Columbia Corporate Registry (BC Registries and Online Services) - corporate name approval through BC Registries Online, with coordinated federal NUANS name-search review via Corporations Canada for extra-provincial operations and integration through the OneStop Business Registry (onestop.gov.bc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A B.C. business corporation name must be in English or French using Latin characters and may include numerals. The name comprises a distinctive element, an optional descriptive element, and a mandatory legal element ('Limited', 'Incorporated', 'Corporation', 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', or French equivalents 'Limitée' / 'Ltée'). A romanized transliteration of a foreign-language name is acceptable as the distinctive element, but the legal element must remain in English or French. A non-Latin-script trademark or trade name may only be registered as an extra-provincial or trade name, not as the statutory corporate name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any word calculated to mislead, obscene or scandalous matter, or a name that is confusingly similar to an existing corporate name, trademark, or protected mark and requires prior ministerial approval or the written consent of the affected rights holder.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a name rejection, the applicant may: (1) submit a new name request online with a fresh fee and a revised distinctive element; (2) where the refusal is based on conflict with an existing corporate or trademark name, file the written consent of the existing owner together with a new name-approval request; (3) for sensitive-token refusals, obtain the required regulatory or ministerial endorsement (e.g., consent of the applicable professional regulator or financial authority) and resubmit; (4) request written reasons from BC Registries and file a formal reconsideration with the Director of BC Registries, supplying legal argument and corrected search evidence; and (5) if reconsideration is denied, apply to the Supreme Court of British Columbia for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241. If clearance cannot be obtained before operational deadlines, incorporate as a numbered B.C. company (e.g., '1234567 B.C. Ltd.') and file a subsequent name-change or voluntary alteration application once name approval is secured. A name reservation may be extended for one additional 56-day period if requested before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A B.C. company is statutorily required to maintain a registered office and a records office at a physical address within British Columbia at which process may be served; the registered office may validly be the office of a licensed B.C. registered agent or law firm holding a virtual-office service. However, for AML/CFT and commercial-substance purposes, a virtual-office-only structure is insufficient for a Medium-Risk Enhanced scrap-copper wholesale entity seeking documentary LC and Swift/TT banking rails, municipal scrap-metal dealer licensing, and FINTRAC compliance. The entity should maintain a physical leased or owned operating office or yard in British Columbia with staff, records, and operational infrastructure proportionate to the stated cross-border consignment business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 25% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by municipal business-license officials or Consumer Protection BC scrap-metal compliance officers; less than 5% risk of a B.C. Corporate Registry physical inspection; the likelihood rises to approximately 40-50% if FINTRAC selects the entity for an AML compliance examination or the RCMP conducts a metal-theft prevention sweep.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, ss. 2-15 (incorporation and name), ss. 50-52 (registered office and records office), ss. 128-185 (shares, directors, and officers), and associated Business Corporations Act Regulation and Name Regulation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate and Business Registries Branch, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles filed under the Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a British Columbia business corporation. Common shares may be issued without par value for such consideration as the directors determine. No mandated paid-up capital escrow account is required by the Business Corporations Act; however, if shares are issued for property or past services, directors must comply with fair-value consideration rules and record the valuation in the company's records.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the subscription for 100 common shares without par value by the founding shareholder be accepted and issued upon payment of full consideration; (2) the registered office and records office be fixed at [address] as described in the Notice of Articles; (3) [A] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, [B] Chief Financial Officer, and [C] Corporate Secretary, serving until successors are elected; (4) the officers be authorized to open corporate bank accounts and execute banking resolutions; and (5) the corporate seal be adopted as affixed to these minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries Corporate Online Portal, Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search through BC Registries' Corporate Online name request function or obtain a NUANS Name Search Report. Verify the proposed name against the Business Corporations Act name requirements and conflicting names. If the desired name is unavailable or not required, choose a numbered company format. Pay the name reservation fee and secure 56-day name protection.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered company election
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name request is refused, the applicant may resubmit with an amended or alternative name or request reconsideration by the Registrar of Companies within the applicable response period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate and Business Registries Branch, BC Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles using Corporate Online or approved software. Specify class and attributes of shares, set registered office address in British Columbia, list the initial directors, and attach director consents. Ensure delivery and records address details comply with the Business Corporations Act.
required_dossiers: Director and officer personal identifier information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned for correction, revise the deficient Notice of Articles and resubmit within the registry's deficiency response period; filing date priority is lost until resubmission is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prepared Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles through Corporate Online. Pay the electronic filing fee of CAD 350 and attach the director consents. Confirm data entry is error-free before submission because amendment post-filing requires additional forms and fees.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues an incomplete filing notification, respond with the requested statutory records or corrected data within the stated deadline or pay an expedited correction fee to obtain same-day processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After processing, retrieve the electronic Certificate of Incorporation from Corporate Online. Verify the legal name, incorporation date, BC company number, and registered office. Retain a certified copy in the corporate minute book and use the company number for all regulatory filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical error or is lost, apply to the Registrar for a certificate of correction or a certified copy using the registry's correction procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial Board of Directors of the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first directors' meeting or sign a written consent resolution. Approve the issue of shares to the founding shareholder, adopt the form of corporate seal, confirm the registered office and records office, appoint the first officers, authorize banking arrangements, and set the company's financial year end. Record all decisions in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an appointed officer or director declines the role, the board may appoint a substitute officer by further resolution and update any director record filed with the registrar if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Federal and Provincial Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; BC Ministry of Finance, Corporation Taxation Branch; WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a federal Business Number through CRA's Business Registration Online. Register for GST/HST, BC Provincial Sales Tax, and, if hiring employees, payroll source deductions and WorkSafeBC workers' compensation coverage. Complete the registrations promptly to avoid penalties for late registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or BC tax authority queries a registration, provide the requested corporate documents and explanation within 30 days; late registration penalties and interest may apply but can be reduced through voluntary disclosure before assessment where eligibility is met.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Business Licence and Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Business Licensing Department of the local city or regional district
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence covering wholesale distribution and recycling of non-ferrous scrap metal. Provide zoning approval, premises floor plan, proof of legal entity, and, where required, a scrap metal dealer licence under local bylaw. Comply with storage limitations, security, and waste handling conditions attached to the licence.
required_dossiers: Site floor plan and storage laydown area description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal licence is denied due to zoning, apply for a variance, temporary use permit, or relocation of operations; appeal the denial to the applicable Property Use and Variance Appeal Board or review tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Environmental Protection Division, British Columbia Ministry of Environment; local municipal business licensing authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Environmental Management Act Waste Discharge Authorization and Recycling Regulation Registration for a Non-Ferrous Scrap Metal Sorting and Shredding Facility

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment, Environmental Protection Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration or Operational Authorization under the Environmental Management Act; a full Environmental Assessment Certificate is generally not required for a low-throughput scrap metal sorting and baling facility below the thresholds in the Reviewable Projects Regulation, but a site-specific emissions and stormwater registration is mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater and stormwater discharges must meet the BC Environmental Management Act and local municipal sewer bylaws, including pH 6.0-9.0, total suspended solids limits, and copper concentration discharge limits applicable to metal recycling operations. Fugitive dust, particulate matter, and volatile organic compound emissions must not exceed provincial ambient air quality objectives; all shredded copper wire stockpiles must be stored on an impermeable pad with secondary containment and covered or wetted to prevent wind dispersal and uncontrolled runoff.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification under the BC Fire Code; municipal building inspection and structural load certification for shredding equipment, storage racks, and mezzanines; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance covering machine guarding, lockout procedures, dust control, noise exposure, manual materials handling, and emergency response planning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – GST/HST registration and Business Number issuance via My Business Account portal; British Columbia Ministry of Finance – Provincial Sales Tax administration via eTaxBC portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) and, if applicable, a GST/HST account. Application is made online via My Business Account (with appropriate authorization), by mail, or by fax using Form RC1, 'Request for a Business Number'. The entity must provide corporate documents, proof of non-resident status, and details of Canadian commercial activities. If conducting taxable activities in British Columbia, a separate PST account must be obtained through the Province of BC's eTaxBC system, supported by statutory declaration and business identification documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Canadian business corporation is subject to entity-level federal and provincial income tax. Available statutory elections include the GST/HST closely related corporation election under section 156 of the Excise Tax Act, the functional currency election under subsection 261(2) of the Income Tax Act, and the annual corporate tax year election under section 249.1. No US-style check-the-box regime exists; hybrid mismatch rules in sections 12.5 and 12.6 of the Income Tax Act may restrict certain entity classification outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) and British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated supplies) over any 12-month period; PST: no small-supplier threshold for registration, required as soon as the entity carries on business or makes taxable sales in British Columbia.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control regime. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically via a CRA-approved service provider or directly through My Business Account. British Columbia PST returns are due through eTaxBC. There is no statutory API-based invoice clearance mandate, but suppliers must issue tax invoices containing the supplier's Business Number, GST/HST registration number, and, where applicable, PST registration number, and must retain electronic records for audit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of shredded non-ferrous scrap copper wire qualifies as zero-rated under section 10 of Part V of Schedule IX to the Excise Tax Act when the goods are sold and delivered outside Canada. The supplier must retain documentary evidence establishing that the goods were physically exported, typically through a common carrier or by direct shipment, and that the sale was made to a non-resident purchaser. The GST/HST registrant may then claim input tax credits on purchased inputs and apply for net refunds where eligible.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits zero-rated export claims by requiring contemporaneous evidence of physical export and foreign payment. Failure to substantiate may result in disallowed zero-rating, reassessment of GST/HST, interest, and penalties. Civil penalties include up to 20% of any net tax amount for false statements or omissions, plus a separate $10,000 penalty for failure to provide documents. Willful evasion of GST or fraudulent export claims may lead to criminal prosecution, fines up to double the tax evaded, and imprisonment. Retrospective clawbacks are permissible within the normal reassessment period, which is generally four years, or without time limit in cases of misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, or wilful default.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) — no separate central foreign-exchange administration; OSFI, FINTRAC, and CBSA exercise auxiliary regulatory and reporting mandates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a market-determined floating exchange rate with full convertibility on both current and capital accounts. There are no statutory exchange controls, no central bank approval hurdles for profit remittance, dividend distribution, or capital repatriation, and no distinction between resident and non-resident capital movements for FX approval purposes. Payments in CAD or foreign currency must be made through a Canadian chartered bank or an authorized foreign bank branch. Transactions equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000 are reportable to FINTRAC as large cash or electronic funds transfer reports. Cross-border dividend and profit remittances are subject to Canadian withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, but not to FX authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose any statutory surrender or conversion timeline on export proceeds. Exporters may retain receivables in any convertible currency or hold them in foreign-currency accounts. Mandatory compliance arises solely through customs/statistical channels: exports of shredded non-ferrous scrap copper wire must be reported to the Canada Border Services Agency via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CAED) when the shipment value exceeds the applicable threshold (CAD 2,000 for most destinations; CAD 2,500 for shipments to the United States). The export declaration must identify the commodity, net weight, value, and HS code 7404.00. Export proceeds should be reconciled with CAED filings to satisfy income tax and transfer-pricing documentation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
Bank of Montreal (BMO Bank of Montreal)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium (conditional). Offshore digital EMIs licensed in the UK, EU, or Singapore may be used for ancillary FX conversion and cross-border remittance, but they cannot serve as the primary CAD clearing or escrow account and are not eligible for documentary letter-of-credit issuance. Such entities must register as Money Service Businesses with FINTRAC before offering remittance services to Canadian clients. For trade settlement, escrow, or high-value clearing involving recycled scrap copper wire, a Canadian Schedule I bank is required.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is accepted by most Schedule I banks for Canadian-incorporated corporations with all directors and beneficial owners located in low-risk jurisdictions. However, for a Medium-Risk_Enhanced trading sector such as scrap copper trading, at least one director or authorized signatory may be required to attend an in-person or notarized video KYC interview at the opening branch or via a credit-union-approved virtual session. The final mandate depends on bank policy; the majority of tier-1 banks permit video-verified remote opening accompanied by notarized corporate documents and enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags — inconsistent weight, value, HS classification, or geographic routing of shredded copper scrap shipments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent assay certificate from an ISO/IEC 17025-accredited laboratory; original commercial invoices in USD/CAD; packing list; weighbridge tickets or bill-of-lading showing net and gross weights; HS code 7404.00 declaration; cargo photographs; supplier contract and purchase order explaining unit-price variance; and transport route documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure — any counterparty, ultimate beneficial owner, or correspondent bank appearing on OFAC, OSFI, or Canadian SEMA sanctions lists, or located in a high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OSFI/SEMA sanctions screening results for all transaction parties and banks; OFAC SDN match clearance; end-user certificate and anti-boycott declaration; country-of-export/import documentation; routing through a non-sanctioned correspondent; and a written opinion from Canadian trade counsel confirming no controlled goods or technical data restrictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually rapid transaction velocity for a newly incorporated entity — multiple cross-border wires, transfers, or LC presentations within 90 days of account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution limiting treasury authority and payment velocity; business plan with projected monthly trade volumes; letters of intent or purchase orders from end-buyers; pro-forma cash flow and financial statements; prior corporate bank reference from the jurisdiction of incorporation; CRA program number; and GST/HST registration evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership opacity or complex beneficial ownership structure requiring third-party verification under British Columbia corporate registry rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extract from BC Corporate Online (BC Registrar) confirming no privacy-shielded persons; corporate organizational chart showing all 25%+ ownership; passport/ID copies and proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declaration; certificate of no prior AML convictions from each owner's jurisdiction; and notarized copies of trust deeds or partnership agreements if applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from non-resident shareholders must be initiated as SWIFT MT103 or SWIFT gpi payments to the corporate's CAD operating or escrow account at a Canadian Schedule I bank. The beneficiary must be identified by full legal name, SWIFT/BIC, and Canadian account number. The remittance information field must clearly state 'unsolicited share capital contribution / free capital injection' and reference the corporate's legal name and account number; do not use commodity or trade descriptions to avoid misclassification as trade receivables. For injections greater than CAD 10,000, the receiving bank must file a FINTRAC EFT report. If the corporation issues shares for the injection, a CRA Schedule 50 or corporate records entry must document the paid-up capital. The originator's bank account name must match the shareholder's legal name to satisfy source-of-wealth verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for cross-border purchases of shredded non-ferrous scrap copper wire may be executed using SWIFT MT103 for telegraphic transfers or through commercial letters of credit. The Canadian bank issues the LC (MT700/MT710) in favour of the overseas seller; the confirming or advising bank negotiates documents; settlement occurs via MT103 or local clearing after compliance presentation. For TT payment, the corporate must provide a purpose narrative referencing the purchase contract, invoice date, cargo description 'shredded non-ferrous scrap copper wire', HS code 7404.00, country of origin, and shipment port. CAD payments use Lynx or Retail Settlement; USD payments clear over Fedwire/CHIPS via the Canadian bank's USD correspondent network. All trade disbursements must be supported by commercial invoices, transport documents, and evidence of goods received to satisfy FINTRAC and customs reporting obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts with a Canadian Schedule I bank, settled via CLS or Payments Canada, used to hedge non-ferrous scrap sales proceeds.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or less-liquid currencies such as CNY, INR, or BRL, used only when the underlying trade settlement currency is not freely deliverable.
Cross-currency swaps (CAD against USD or EUR) to convert foreign-currency operating liabilities into CAD term funding while stabilizing cash flow.
Plain vanilla European-style FX options (call or put) purchased for hedging purposes only, with no speculative option-writing, subject to bank limits and derivatives qualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report under section 51 of the Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies (BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation, each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100 (approx USD 74); continued non-filing for two consecutive years permits administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Registrar

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Directors' and members' register update, and corporate records retention attestation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies via statutory records maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Registers and minute books updated within 10 business days of any change; reviewed annually as part of the annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under the BCBCA; fines may be imposed, and incomplete registers reduce evidentiary weight and impair financing or asset sale transactions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold automatically triggers an audit for a private BC company; a distributing or offering corporation must appoint an independent auditor, and a shareholder-requisitioned audit is compulsory under the BCBCA. Private companies may waive auditor appointment by unanimous shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for distributing or public companies; ASPE or IFRS for private companies as selected by the directors and applied consistently. The Canada Revenue Agency also requires books and records supporting all tax reporting under the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO filing is currently required for a private BC company. The BC annual report confirms director details but does not require share-by-share beneficial ownership reporting. Share transfers and significant control changes must be reflected promptly in the register of members and register of directors. Federal CBCA corporations file a separate Individuals with Significant Control annual confirmation; phased BC Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act obligations should be monitored for future filings.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - USD 500 per year for registered office and corporate agent services in British Columbia
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 10,000 per year for a small-to-medium BC private company with high-volume scrap metal transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27.00% combined (Federal Part I 15.00% + British Columbia provincial 12.00%) for general corporate income; BC small-business rate 2.00% combined with federal SBD rate 9.00% yields 11.00% on first CA$500,000 qualifying active income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays for a BC business corporation. Deductions/incentives: Science Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit (15% non-refundable; 35% refundable for qualifying CCPC up to CA$3M expenditure); BC SR&ED refundable credit (10% of eligible expenditures); accelerated Capital Cost Allowance on Class 43/Class 29 manufacturing equipment; 100% CCA on UCC for certain clean energy/zero-emission vehicles (Class 54/55); British Columbia provincial M&P rate 8% where qualifying manufacturing/processing occurs; active business income of CCPC eligible for SBD is not available for a private corporation that is not a CCPC (public/foreign-controlled), and trading income from cross-border consignment generally remains at general rate.
